<objective>
Widen the tracer's create-and-lock worktree slice into the full WT-01…WT-07 lifecycle: idempotent
provisioning that survives a crash, `.fleet.yml` setup commands under the worker's own environment, and
teardown that captures dirty work before it removes anything.

Purpose: the tracer assumes a clean first run. Real operation does not — a daemon restart mid-provision
leaves a branch without a registration, or a directory without either. ARCHITECTURE.md §4's four-step
algorithm is what makes `ensureWorktree()` safe to call again, which is exactly what Phase 3's crash
reconciliation will need. And WT-07's dirty-capture-before-teardown is the difference between an agent's
work being inspectable and being silently destroyed.

Output: a `worktree-manager.ts` that converges from any partial state, runs setup commands safely, and
never discards work.
</objective>

  <name>Task 1: Implement the four-step idempotent ensureWorktree algorithm and collision handling</name>
  <files>src/runner/worktree-manager.ts, src/runner/worktree-manager.test.ts</files>
  <read_first>
    - src/runner/worktree-manager.ts (from plan 02-04 — the current create-and-lock implementation this task replaces)

    - src/registry/fleet-yaml.ts (lines 60-105 — the total-function, never-throw discipline: a structured result for every failure mode rather than a propagating throw)
    - src/registry/registry.test.ts (the scratch-repo `git()` helper shape to reuse for fixtures)
    - src/spikes/scratch-repo.ts (the `withScratchRepo` lifecycle: mkdtemp, init, commit, rmSync in `finally`)
    - .planning/research/ARCHITECTURE.md (§4 — the worktree lifecycle spine and the four-step algorithm this task implements verbatim)
    - .planning/phases/02-execution-worktree-runner-billing-safety/02-RESEARCH.md (Pattern 3 — every git worktree subcommand's exact verified behavior and exit code against git 2.55.0)
  </read_first>
  <behavior>
    - State A (nothing exists): `ensureWorktree()` creates the branch and the worktree via `add -b` and locks it.
    - State B (already registered and on the correct branch): `ensureWorktree()` returns the existing `ProvisionResult` without running `add` at all; `git worktree list --porcelain` still shows exactly one entry for that path.
    - State C (branch exists, worktree not registered): `ensureWorktree()` re-attaches with `git worktree add <path> <branch>` — WITHOUT `-b` — and succeeds. Attempting `add -b` in this state fails with exit 255 and the message `a branch named '<branch>' already exists`, so the implementation must not reach that call.
    - State D (directory exists on disk but is not registered): `ensureWorktree()` removes the stray directory, then retries. `git worktree list --porcelain` shows the entry as `prunable gitdir file points to non-existent location` before the prune.
    - State E (branch exists AND is checked out by an unrelated worktree): a numeric suffix is appended (`fleet/<short-id>-2`) and provisioning succeeds; nothing throws.
    - Locking is idempotent: `ensureWorktree()` called twice yields porcelain output containing exactly one `locked ` line for that path.
    - `git worktree remove <path>` against a locked worktree exits 128 with `cannot remove a locked working tree`; the manager never calls it while locked and always unlocks first.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Replace the tracer's minimal `ensureWorktree()` in `src/runner/worktree-manager.ts` with D-19's full
four-step algorithm, implemented verbatim from ARCHITECTURE.md §4 and validated against RESEARCH.md
Pattern 3's session-verified observations:

**Step 1** — run `git worktree prune` unconditionally first. It is idempotent and cheap, and it
normalizes stale administrative entries left by a manually-deleted directory. RESEARCH.md confirmed
`prune` removes exactly that administrative entry and nothing else — it does NOT delete the branch, which
survives independently of worktree registration.

**Step 2** — run `git worktree list --porcelain` and parse it into a structured list. The porcelain
format is `worktree <absolute-path>`, `HEAD <sha>`, `branch refs/heads/<name>`, and, only when locked, a
`locked <reason>` line. Write a small exported `parseWorktreePorcelain(output)` returning
`Array<{ path, head, branch, lockReason }>` so the parsing is unit-testable without git. If an entry
already exists for the target path AND its `branch` matches the expected `refs/heads/fleet/<short-id>`,
this is state B: return the existing result without running `add`. If an entry exists for the target
path but on a DIFFERENT branch, treat it as a stray: unlock, remove, and fall through.

**Step 3** — when the branch exists (check with `git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<branch>`) but no
registration does, run `git worktree add <path> <baseRefOrBranch>` WITHOUT `-b`. RESEARCH.md verified
this succeeds and checks out the existing branch cleanly, and that `add -b` on an existing branch name
fails with exit 255 — so branching on the branch's existence before choosing the form is the whole point,
not a fallback after catching an error.

**Step 4** — when the target directory exists on disk but is not registered, `rmSync(path, { recursive: true, force: true })`
it and retry the appropriate `add` form. Only a directory strictly under the Fleet-owned worktree root
returned by `worktreeRootFor()` may be removed this way; assert that containment before the `rmSync` and
throw `WorktreeError('worktree_path_outside_root')` otherwise.

**Collision handling (D-20)** — an existing branch is state C's retry case, never an error. Only when the
branch exists AND `git worktree list --porcelain` shows it checked out at a path that is not this task's
target path is a collision genuine; in that case append `-2`, then `-3`, incrementing until an unused
name is found, and record the chosen name in the returned `ProvisionResult`. Cap the search at 100
attempts and throw `WorktreeError('branch_name_exhausted')` beyond it rather than looping forever.

**Locking (D-21)** — locking stays part of provisioning, not a separate call site: `git worktree lock`
runs immediately after every successful `add`, with the reason string `fleet task <taskId>`. When the
porcelain output already shows a `locked ` line for the path, treat the lock as already-satisfied and do
not re-issue it — a second `lock` on a locked tree exits non-zero. There must be no window in which an
active worktree is unlocked, which is what makes a prune structurally unable to delete live state.

Follow `fleet-yaml.ts`'s total-function discipline: a git failure the algorithm expects (branch already
exists, tree already locked) is caught and branched on, never allowed to propagate as an unhandled throw.
A genuinely unexpected git failure throws `WorktreeError` with the captured stderr in its message.

Do NOT enable `extensions.worktreeConfig` and do NOT run `git config --worktree` — D-05 explicitly
rejects per-worktree config poisoning because it is a persistent mutation of a repository Fleet does not
own. Do NOT pass `--no-track` or unset `branch.<name>.remote`: RESEARCH.md Pitfall 4 verified the
tracking-config side effect of cutting from a remote-tracking ref is harmless to correctness and
security, and CONTEXT.md defers its cleanup to `fleet gc`.

Extend `src/runner/worktree-manager.test.ts` with fixtures that construct each of states A–E in a real
scratch repo (a bare "remote" plus a clone, matching RESEARCH.md Pattern 3's verified sequence), and
assert the `<behavior>` list. These tests need real `git` but no `claude`, no network, and no auth.
  </action>

  </verify>

    - A test asserts `parseWorktreePorcelain()` correctly extracts a `lockReason` from a `locked fleet task <id>` line and returns `undefined` for an unlocked entry.
    - A test asserts `ensureWorktree()` throws `WorktreeError` with code `worktree_path_outside_root` when asked to clear a directory outside `worktreeRootFor()`'s root.
    - `grep -rn "worktreeConfig\|config --worktree\|pushurl" src/runner/` returns no matches.

  <done>`ensureWorktree()` converges on one locked worktree on the correct branch from any of five starting states, and handles a genuine branch collision without crashing.</done>

  </read_first>
  <behavior>
    - A `.fleet.yml` with `setup: ['echo hello > setup-ran.txt']` results in `setup-ran.txt` existing inside the worktree before any spawn.
    - A setup command's spawned environment contains only allowlisted keys — asserted by a setup command that dumps its own environment to a file inside the worktree, then reading that file back.
    - A setup command exiting non-zero returns a structured failure naming the command string and carrying its combined stdout/stderr; provisioning does not continue.
    - A setup command that never exits is terminated at its own per-command timeout and reported as a failure, not left hanging.
    - A repository with no `.fleet.yml`, or one whose `setup` key is absent or an empty array, provisions successfully and runs zero commands.
    - A setup command containing shell metacharacters is passed as a single argv element and is never string-concatenated with any taREDACTED_SECRET value.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Add an exported `runSetupCommands({ worktreePath, repoPath, taskId, timeoutMs })` to
`src/runner/worktree-manager.ts`, called from `ensureWorktree()` AFTER add-and-lock and BEFORE the spawn
(D-24's ordering), and wire `ensureWorktree()` to invoke it.

Read the commands by calling `readFleetYml(repoPath)` at this moment — live, never snapshotted (Phase 1
D-17) — and iterate `config.setup ?? []`. Do not re-parse the YAML and do not re-declare the schema;
`src/registry/fleet-yaml.ts` already owns both.

Execute each command as `spawnSync('sh', ['-c', cmd], { cwd: worktreePath, env: buildWorkerEnv({ ... }), shell: false, timeout, encoding: 'utf8' })`.
Three properties matter and each has a reason:
- `env: buildWorkerEnv(...)` — the SAME allowlisted environment the worker gets, never the daemon's
  ambient environment. A setup command is just as capable of leaking a credential into the tree as the
  agent is, so D-24 gives it the same starvation.
- `shell: false` with `sh` invoked via an argv array — `sh -c` is itself the shell, but it is reached
  through argv rather than through Node's own `shell: true`, so no profile file is re-sourced and no
  second layer of shell interpretation is applied.
- `cmd` is a SINGLE argv element taken verbatim from the parsed YAML. Never build it by string
  interpolation with a task title, prompt, id, or path. The project's own `.fleet.yml` is trusted input
  by design; taREDACTED_SECRET data is not, and must never reach this position.

Give each command its own timeout, defaulting to 300000 ms and overridable via the resolved runner
config. A non-zero exit or a timeout returns a structured `{ ok: false, command, output, reason }` — do
not throw from the loop. `ensureWorktree()` translates that into a `WorktreeError` with code
`setup_command_failed` carrying the command and the first 4096 characters of its combined output, so the
caller records `CRASH` with that payload and the task lands in `failed`. Dispatching an agent into a
half-provisioned worktree is the failure mode this prevents.

Extend `src/runner/worktree-manager.test.ts` for every `<behavior>` case. For the environment-shape
assertion, use a setup command that writes `env` output to a file inside the worktree and then read and
parse that file — this proves the property at the real spawn boundary rather than by inspecting the
object Fleet intended to pass.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>npm test -- src/runner/worktree-manager.test.ts</automated>
  </verify>
  <acceptance_criteria>

    - A test asserts the setup file was created BEFORE the spawn by checking it exists at the point `ensureWorktree()` returns.
    - `npm test` (whole `unit` project) exits 0.
  </acceptance_criteria>
  <done>Project setup commands run inside the worktree under the worker's own starved environment, and a failure stops provisioning instead of half-provisioning.</done>
